title: AI yet to make significant dent in German employment, study finds
source_used: Yahoo Finance page carrying a wire report on the IAB study (1,054 characters, full text read)
key_facts: A report by the Nuremberg-based Institute for Employment Research (IAB), released on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, found AI has yet to cost Germany a significant number of jobs, but younger workers may already be affected.
Full-time employment in occupations heavily influenced by AI has developed better since 2022 than in other occupations.

Employment growth in AI-affected occupations was almost six percentage points higher among 30- to 39-year-olds and around five points higher among 40- to 64-year-olds than in less AI-affected occupations.
For workers under 30, full-time employment in heavily AI-affected occupations fell 1.2 percentage points more than in less affected jobs.

IAB researchers see fundamental risks from AI in industry, particularly in non-academic occupations, and say employment among young people tends to develop negatively when the influence of AI is already high.
The photo caption describes the IAB as the Institute for Employment Research of the Federal Employment Agency; the photo is credited to dpa.
quote_evidence: Artificial intelligence (AI) is yet to cost Germany a significant number of jobs, a report by the Nuremberg-based Institute for Employment Research (IAB) has found - but younger workers may already be affected.
However, the picture is negative for those under 30: full-time employment in this age group in occupations heavily affected by AI fell 1.2 percentage points more than in less affected jobs, it said.
IAB researchers see fundamental risks from AI in industry, particularly in non-academic occupations.
why_it_matters_hint: German data so far show no broad job loss to AI, but a weakness among workers under 30 in the most AI-affected occupations.
notes: Yahoo Finance is a copy site; the text has no byline and only the photo is credited to dpa, so the wire agency is likely dpa but is not stated for the text. The original IAB report was not opened. The comparison is between more and less AI-affected occupations, not proof of cause.
